university-at-albany-suny.faculty: William Kennedy, the 1984 Pulitzer Prize winner for fiction ("Ironweed") and a longtime UAlbany creative-writing professor (full professor from 1983), founded the university's New York State Writers Institute in 1983 and remains listed as its founder. (Faculty change — verify current active-teaching status given his age.)

research.undergrad: The Minerva Center for High-Impact Practices coordinates undergraduate research across UAlbany's nine schools/colleges, including STEP/CSTEP programs, summer research, and a Presidential Award for Undergraduate Research.
research.areas: Notable research centers include the RNA Institute, the Cancer Research Center, and the Atmospheric Sciences Research Center; UAlbany is classified R1 (very high research activity).

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity; roughly $246 million in annual research expenditures (FY2021).
research.areas: Signature facility is the International Hurricane Research Center, the only university-based tropical-storm research facility of its kind in the U.S., home to the Wall of Wind — an NSF-recognized experimental facility (since 2015) able to simulate Category 5 hurricane conditions.

chapman-university.faculty: Vernon L. Smith, 2002 Nobel laureate in Economic Sciences (pioneer of experimental economics), is a current professor of economics and law at Chapman, where he founded the Economic Science Institute. Yakir Aharonov, the James J. Farley Professor of Natural Philosophy, co-discovered the Aharonov–Bohm effect, shared the 1998 Wolf Prize in Physics, received the 2009 National Medal of Science, and was elected a Foreign Member of the Royal Society in 2024; he has taught at Chapman since 2008. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.undergrad: The Center for Undergraduate Excellence coordinates a Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF), credit-bearing Student-Faculty Research and Creative Activity courses (291/491), Scholarly/Creative and Travel Grants, and mentorship programs like "Lunch with a Professor," with work showcased at the Student Scholar Symposium.
research.areas: Examples include undergraduate-led biomaterial development for tissue repair; broader institutional strengths include the Economic Science Institute (experimental economics) and computation/complex-systems centers within Schmid College.

fashion-institute-of-technology.faculty: Valerie Steele, director and chief curator of The Museum at FIT since 2003, is a widely cited fashion historian and author of numerous books on the history and theory of fashion. (Faculty/role change — verify.)

research.undergrad: In place of traditional lab research, FIT students engage through specialized studios (photography, sculpture, printmaking, model-making), annual BFA fashion shows, and Gallery FIT, which hosts student and faculty exhibitions.

research.level: R2: Doctoral Universities – High research activity
research.undergrad: The Robert H. "Bob" Bell Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurial Development provides entrepreneurship training and support for student ventures.
research.areas: The Center for Functional Nanoscale Measures (CFNM) has produced more Black PhDs in nanoscale science than any other HBCU, an advanced-materials research strength. The graduate social work program is nationally ranked.

research.undergrad: The Prescott campus offers Ignite Grants (up to $48,000 annually per project for student research under a faculty mentor) and Eagle-Prize (E-Prize) Grants ($60,000 distributed annually to student teams in design/research competitions).
research.areas: Aerospace-focused research including the Aerospace Research and Technology Park and the FAA NextGen Florida Test Bed (Daytona Beach), and the Robertson Safety Institute with its Crash Lab and Aviation Safety and Security Archives (Prescott).

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research spending and doctorate production

research.undergrad: GREAT Day (Geneseo Recognizing Excellence, Achievement, and Talent) is an annual, college-wide, classes-cancelled symposium where students present research, scholarship, and creative work across posters, papers, performances, and film.
research.areas: Geneseo is a member of the New York Space Grant Consortium and receives NASA grants supporting space-related undergraduate research.

clemson-university.faculty: Trudy Mackay, Director of Clemson's Center for Human Genetics and Self Family Endowed Chair of Human Genetics, is a member of the National Academy of Sciences (elected 2010) and the National Academy of Medicine, and won the 2016 Wolf Prize in Agriculture for her work in quantitative genetics, including establishing the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity
research.areas: The Clemson University International Center for Automotive Research (CU-ICAR) in Greenville is a major automotive-engineering research park; the Charleston Innovation Campus houses offshore wind-turbine testing facilities and the Warren Lasch Conservation Center.

university-of-houston.faculty: Paul C. W. Chu, Professor of Physics and T.L.L. Temple Chair of Science, is a National Medal of Science recipient and founding director of the Texas Center for Superconductivity; he is known for helping discover high-temperature superconductivity in 1987 and continues to publish on superconductivity at ambient pressure. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity
research.areas: More than 40 research centers spanning nanotechnology, superconductivity, space commercialization, biomedical sciences, energy, and AI; the university's "50in5" initiative (launched 2018) aims to raise research expenditures 50% and double its national research centers within five years.

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity; research programs bring in more than $822 million annually to the region and support roughly 23,100 local jobs.
research.areas: Historic strength in biomedicine: Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine at Pitt's Virus Research Lab (declared effective 1955), and Thomas Starzl established Pitt as a world leader in organ transplantation in the 1980s.

research.level: R2: Doctoral Universities – High research activity
research.areas: Research is concentrated in Creighton's professional schools (medicine, dentistry, law, nursing, pharmacy); the university also holds Space-Grant status through the National Space Grant College and Fellowship Program.

university-of-california-santa-cruz.faculty: David Haussler, Distinguished Professor of Biomolecular Engineering and founding scientific director of the UC Santa Cruz Genomics Institute, led the team that assembled the first human genome sequence and developed the widely used UCSC Genome Browser; he is a member of both the National Academy of Sciences (2006) and National Academy of Engineering (2018). (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: UC Santa Cruz faculty include 16 members of the National Academy of Sciences and 29 fellows of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.
research.areas: Genomics (UCSC Genome Browser, Human Genome Project contributions), astronomy through administrative oversight of Lick Observatory, adaptive optics (NSF-funded center), and organic agriculture through the nation's oldest university organic-farm program.

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity
research.areas: The School of Medicine is known for pioneering transplant surgery, including the first fully self-contained artificial heart transplant and the first successful hand transplantation in the United States.

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity; $211 million in R&D expenditure (NSF, 2018)
research.areas: Notable research includes molecular sensing technology and flame-retardant polymer development. The English department has hosted Pulitzer Prize-winning and poet-laureate-level writers historically (e.g., James Tate, Ted Hughes), though current creative-writing faculty should be checked directly given turnover.

research.level: Research and development expenditures were $542 million in fiscal year 2019, ranking 48th nationally and second in Virginia (NSF).
research.undergrad: The Fralin Life Science Institute runs named undergraduate research programs: the First-Year Fralin Undergraduate program, the Fralin Undergraduate Research Fellowship, and the Fralin Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship, covering vector-borne and infectious disease, plant sciences, cancer biology, and ecology.
research.areas: Agriculture and biotechnology, ICT, transportation, energy (fuel cells, power electronics), and security/sustainability engineering.

university-of-california-riverside.faculty: Richard R. Schrock, who shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (for olefin metathesis) while at MIT, joined UC Riverside's faculty in 2018 and now holds the George K. Helmkamp Founder's Chair of Chemistry there. (Faculty change — verify; note his Nobel-era affiliation was MIT, not UCR.)

research.level: Since 1997, more than 110 UCR faculty have been elected AAAS fellows; seven current or former faculty have been elected to the National Academy of Sciences, and more than 50 have received Guggenheim Fellowships. Research expenditure was $167.8 million in FY2018.
research.areas: Agricultural science has historically represented over half of UCR's research spending, anchored by the Agricultural Experiment Station and the Center for Environmental Research and Technology.

research.undergrad: The Material Lab and Center for Sustainable Design Strategies gives students hands-on access to materials research within the engineering building.
research.areas: The Pratt Center for Community Development, founded by the urban planning department in 1963, applies student and faculty research to neighborhood revitalization in Brooklyn and beyond.

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity; $186 million in R&D expenditure (NSF, 2018)
research.areas: The Institute of Energy Conversion is the world's oldest solar-energy research institute (est. 1972; thin-film solar cells); the Delaware Environmental Institute (2009) covers environmental science and policy; the UD Energy Institute (2008) has received multi-million-dollar annual grants for advanced solar research.

research.level: 27 NJIT faculty have been elected to the National Academy of Inventors (17 Fellows, 10 Senior Members) as of 2025; R&D expenditure was $162 million (NSF, 2018).
research.undergrad: NJIT participates in the McNair Scholars Program (since 1999), preparing underrepresented undergraduates for doctoral study.
research.areas: Applied mathematics and materials science, biomedical engineering, cybersecurity, nanotechnology/polymer science, and solar-terrestrial physics — the latter anchored by the university's operation of the Big Bear Solar Observatory and Owens Valley Solar Array.

rutgers-university.faculty: David Case, Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Chemistry, is a National Academy of Sciences member recognized for contributions to computational chemistry and structural biology; as emeritus he is no longer active day-to-day teaching faculty. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity
research.areas: The Waksman Institute of Microbiology, founded 1954 by Nobel laureate Selman Waksman (discoverer of streptomycin), remains an active Rutgers research institute on microbial, developmental, and plant molecular genetics. The Rutgers University Center for Cognitive Science draws faculty from psychology, linguistics, computer science, philosophy, and electrical engineering.

university-at-buffalo-suny.faculty: Deborah D. L. Chung, SUNY Distinguished Professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (on the faculty since 1986), directs the Composite Materials Research Laboratory and is known for pioneering interface-area-based design of electromagnetic-interference shielding materials and self-sensing/self-healing structural materials. (Faculty change — verify.)

research.level: R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity; total research expenditures were $401 million in FY2017, with a projected $540 million by 2026.
research.areas: UB hosts two New York State Centers of Excellence, in bioinformatics and in materials informatics.
